advice: For the general SME path, build tail predicates and offsets from each tile’s remaining element count. For a tile beginning at j, load the second B vector from j + min(VL, n-j), with a predicate covering only the remaining columns after the first VL. Apply the same rule to A’s second row vector and store only active rows and columns. This avoids relying on masked loads to make an out-of-bounds base pointer safe. Keep the existing four ZA tile selectors (0–3), and use a full-tile branch only when both dimensions contain the complete 2VL tile. For n=512, consider a separate constant-loop path only if it is guarded by runtime checks that n is 512 and the full-tile assumptions hold; retain the general path for every other size.
risks: The supplied evidence contains no validated tail-specific failure or measured benefit, so this is correctness hardening advice, not a performance claim. Predicate and pointer-offset mistakes can still corrupt odd tails; the current benchmark evidence also does not establish that a fast path will improve AC scores. Do not attribute any future score change to tail handling without paired controls.
